newsitem.title: UK: Brit Energy signs new contract with BNFL.
newsitem.headline: Brit Energy signs new contract with BNFL.

text.p: Britain's nuclear power generator British Energy Plc said on Wednesday it had concluded new service contracts with British Nuclear Fuels (BNFL) worth around 1.5 billion pounds.
The company also announced its first annual results since flotation last year on June 4. It said in a statement it had made pre-tax profits of 61 million pounds.
Analysts had forecast pretax profits in a range between 57 and 67 million pounds. The firm made a final dividend payment of 9.1 pence per share to make a total of 13.7 pence.
British Energy said the contracts with BNFL cover the extension of AGR fuel fabrication services from 2000 to 2006, with a facility to extend beyond.
"For British Energy, it means that we have contracts in place for all the expected arisings of AGR fuel from NEL and SNL power stations," British Energy chief executive Robert Hawley.

The company said the signing of the contracts, in conjunction with those already in place, means that it now has fixed price contracts covering the bulk of spent fuel services for the whole of the remaining lives of its seven AGR power stations.
